environment.working_tree: Modified worktree (50 paths): Products planning/evidence, Catalog adapter/tests and local migrations; no Supabase remote writes or migration applications.

decisions.summary: Active organization membership and Platform permissions are the authorization source.
Use existing owner/admin/agent/viewer roles, not new ERP roles.
catalog.write is the canonical general Products write permission; remote catalog.manage grants and RLS must be forward-migrated and deployment verified.
Enforce authorization server-side and through database policies, not UI visibility alone.
Organization is the Products access boundary; Products are shared across workspaces within that organization.
Workspace-specific Products authorization is outside this release; legacy workspace values are migration provenance.
No record-assignee/team ACL exists in the current Products domain.
catalog.read includes sales-price visibility; purchase costs require separate cost permissions; export and permanent deletion remain disabled for this release.
Shared Platform collaboration and Document Intelligence permissions are reused and inherit referenced-record access.
Membership and role grants remain Platform organization-management actions.
Remote Products mutations require an immutable Platform audit event in the same transaction; audit failure rejects the mutation.
Separate catalog.cost.read and catalog.cost.manage permissions are granted to owner/admin only by default; agent/viewer receive neither.
The shared Files boundary is approved, but product-media metadata-table policies, signed-preview authorization, detach/retention behavior and end-to-end acceptance remain open.

actions: Reconciled catalog read/write permissions and organization-wide scope with current Platform roles and existing ERP policies.
Added the Product Owner-approved owner/admin-only default grants for catalog.cost.read and catalog.cost.manage.
Separated cost-field access from ordinary catalog projections, search, caches, logs, activity, exports and background processing.
Defined product/SKU association permissions separately from shared Files metadata and Storage permissions.
Audited current catalog, cost-reference, media-association, Storage and Files RLS policies and recorded deployment uncertainty.
Added authorization test cases for cost disclosure, role revocation, tenant boundaries, media access and deletion.
Revalidated the current media migration chain: Storage object deletion is denied for product-media paths, but media metadata tables retain FOR ALL/DELETE policies.
Confirmed the shared append-only audit table/function and approved semantics; Products call sites and atomicity tests remain absent.

validation.evidence: All 34 delivery state-machine and evidence tests passed.
Delivery ledger validation passed: 8 ledgers checked.
Module run validation passed: 110 checkpoint files checked (36 archived legacy records).

validation.command: Review access-model.md against approved decisions and current migration chain
validation.evidence: The Storage-object policy, asset/assignment table policies, shared audit capability and implementation/deployment gaps are distinguished accurately.
No whitespace errors in the access-design revalidation evidence.

requirements.evidence: The original foundation migration grants legacy catalog.manage and its FOR ALL policy permits DELETE through catalog.read; remote forward-state for all ERP tables remains unverified.
Organization-wide visibility is confirmed; legacy workspace IDs need a reviewed migration, and the deployed RLS state remains unverified.
Owner/admin-only catalog.cost.read/manage grants are approved, but shared permission keys, role mappings, cost DTO filtering, adapter checks and RLS have not been implemented.

The shared Files boundary and Storage object-delete hardening are approved/recorded, but media metadata-table FOR ALL policies, signed previews, detach/retention acceptance and full RLS verification remain open.
CRM-owned identities remain under CRM/Platform authorization; ERP does not create duplicate customer permissions.

evidence.result: Defines role/action/scope matrix, cost permissions, shared Files boundary, RLS, audit, test cases and open decisions.

Product-media Storage object reads/writes use catalog permissions and authenticated object deletion excludes product-media paths; these migrations do not replace asset/assignment table FOR ALL policies.
The shared append-only audit table/function and mutation-prevention trigger exist; no Products mutation call site or transaction-atomicity test was found.
PlatformPermission contains catalog.read and catalog.write but no catalog.cost.read/manage permissions.
Cost-reference SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE policies currently use catalog.write; DELETE is revoked.

Association policies use FOR ALL with catalog.write and the migration replaces shared Storage policies; later forward migrations harden product-media object deletion but do not replace these table policies.
Foundation policy uses FOR ALL with catalog.read in USING and catalog.manage in WITH CHECK; deployed state is unverified.
Shared file metadata RLS is based on active organization membership and does not define a files.* permission key.
Current shared Files metadata policy allows active organization members to read/insert/update organization files and has a separate owner/admin/agent delete policy.

next_handoff: 04-api: revalidate cost/media permission-filtered contracts against approved access semantics; keep remote mutation blocked pending RLS, audit integration and deployed-state evidence.
notes: Only owner/admin receive both cost permissions by default; this role selection was confirmed by the Product Owner for this release.
Shared Files boundary and append-only audit semantics are approved; Files lifecycle/metadata-table enforcement and Products audit integration/atomicity tests are incomplete.
Forward permission/RLS migrations and deployed-state verification are required; no database or production policy was changed in this phase.
Legacy workspace/category data requires an authorized dry-run before any production migration.
